title: Seastone Logistics — sandbox VPC adapter onramp discovery
summary: Initial technical discovery for integrating Redwood across Seastone's sandbox and VPC-based environments. Main themes: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs for latency/cost, gateway/proxy architecture for egress control, SDK interoperability with LongChain/LongChain-style adapters and LlamaIndex, rate-limit/tenant quotas, and observability hooks for token-level tracing. Actionables include a pilot plan, security docs, benchmark checklist and a follow-up SE-led sandbox test on their VPC connector.
topics: rate limits, per-tenant quotas and burst policies
security and compliance: SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, SOC2
action_items: Jonah Kim: share Redwood sandbox VPC connector guide + quickstart (2029-06-21)
Maya Patel: send preliminary dedicated capacity pricing and pilot SLA outline (2029-06-20)
Seastone (Priya): provide sample trace and request pattern (anonymized) for benchmark (2029-06-24)
Marcus Lee: confirm internal egress proxy constraints and firewall rules and share with Redwood (2029-06-22)
next_steps: Schedule 60m sandbox test in Seastone VPC with Redwood SE (Jonah) — target week of 2029-06-24
Maya to share security docs (SOC 2 report, SAML SSO steps, KMS integration notes)
Create a lightweight benchmark plan (10k token/day profile) and run hosted vs dedicated latency run
Decide pilot model mix (open quantized + one higher-quality variant) before pilot kickoff
transcript:
Meeting header: 2029-06-17 08:05 PT | Duration 54m | Record: yes
Attendees listed: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (CTO Seastone), Priya S. (Platform), Marcus (SRE), Dana (Procurement), Ben (external consultant)
-- 00:00 Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, we know friday is busy so we'll keep tight agenda, introduce quick then jump into your current stack and constraints
-- 00:18 Alex (Seastone): hey thanks, quick FYI we run most dev/test in a sandbox VPC, prod is a dedicated k8s cluster across two regions, right now inference is mostly internal TF-serving + some on-prem GPU boxes, latency is... not great for chat features, so we're exploring hosted/dedicated/private options
-- 00:38 Jonah (Redwood SE): cool. can you describe the proxy / egress pattern — do you have a single egress gateway or many? also any outbound whitelists?
-- 00:51 Priya (Seastone): we have an egress gateway per cluster, outbound is locked down to allowlist only — we run a strict firewall and sometimes the egress is via a proxy appliance. vendor egress needs a static IP range which is part of why onprem is attractive
-- 01:10 Marcus (SRE): also cost, like we don't want to blow budget for embeddings at scale. we care about token cost but also predictability of throughput.
-- 01:23 Maya: totally. Redwood offers three onramps — hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem. for sandbox evaluation i'd suggest either hosted with proxy allowlisting or our sandbox VPC connector to demo near-prod without changing firewall rules.
-- 01:42 Alex: how intrusive is the sandbox connector? does it require agents inside our VPC or is it a sidecar?
-- 01:50 Jonah: it's generally a connector you can run as a sidecar or kube DaemonSet that opens a controlled outbound tunnel. for sandbox we usually provide a non-prod connector image and a lightweight control plane. important note: the connector supports prefix caching and automatic batching — which helps cost — but caching interacts with PII policies so you'll be able to toggle prefix/K-V cache off in private mode
-- 02:20 Priya: when you say K-V cache you mean the kv cache for autoregressive contexts? we've had people say "K-V cash" before in notes, just clarifying
-- 02:29 Jonah: yes kv cache — sorry for the slur — kv cache also has eviction policies.
-- 02:34 Alex: on SDKs — our devs are building on LongChain and LlamaIndex (we call it Llama Indx internally), can we use Redwood's SDKs without major rewrites?
-- 02:45 Maya: Redwood SDKs provide adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex patterns; there is a simple adapter layer and examples. note: some community libs call it LongChain incorrectly in docs (we've seen that) so we'll share a repo snippet.
-- 03:05 Marcus: Latency vs cost — are the batching knobs manual or auto? we need to preserve <120ms p50 for chat in prod, but background embedding jobs can be batched for cost savings
-- 03:20 Jonah: batching is workload-aware and we expose controls: target latency SLO, max batch size, and a fast-path route for low-latency requests. for dedicated pools you can set reserved concurrency which keeps p50 low. quick caveat: very small sequences can actually be slower in some quantized kernels due to kernel dispatch overhead — we'll show numbers in the benchmark
-- 04:02 Priya: observability — we need token-level tracing, per-tenant cost breakdown, and ability to export traces to our Datadog setup. how does Redwood hook telemetry out?
-- 04:14 Jonah: we emit structured events and spans, token counts per request, and response latencies. for VPC/private deployments we can push to your OTLP collector or S3 for archival. we also have route-level dashboards in the console with trace links — you'll want to pass a request-id header to correlate with your logs
-- 04:43 Alex: security — SOC 2, SAML, KMS, audit logs — what's available for private vs hosted?
-- 04:53 Maya: hosted includes SOC 2 and we offer SAML SSO + RBAC; for private we do customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and encrypted audit logs with longer retention. we'll attach SOC docs and a matrix for differences.
-- 05:10 Dana (Procurement): timeline — if pilot looks good we need procurement terms and a PO within 6 weeks. are there pilot agreements or do we just run on usage credits?
-- 05:20 Maya: pilot can run under a short-term usage agreement with a trial credit or as a billed pilot with committed dedicated hours. we can work both ways.
-- 05:35 Ben (consultant): curious on the gateway pattern: do you recommend sidecar vs outbound proxy for policy enforcement?
-- 05:45 Jonah: sidecar gives app-level observability and automatic request tagging; outbound proxy centralizes egress allowlist and TLS termination. for Seastone with strict firewall the outbound proxy + static IP from Redwood (dedicated) is simplest. for sandbox we recommend sidecar to avoid changing infra.
-- 06:20 Alex: any hard limits on per-tenant quotas? we want to enforce per-team quota and burst policies so one team doesn't exhaust the pool
-- 06:32 Maya: yes we support per-tenant quotas and token budgets. Rate limits are configurable at the route layer and we provide soft and hard caps — soft caps return warnings and hard caps reject. For dedicated pools you can reserve capacity for teams.
-- 06:55 Marcus: how do retries and fallbacks work? if our primary model is busy will you fallback to smaller quantized variant?
-- 07:03 Jonah: yes we support fallback policies by model family. route rules can specify fallback candidates and cost overrides. that said, fallback can affect output consistency so we recommend A/B testing with eval sets before wide rollout.
-- 07:28 Priya: about LlamaIndex compatibility — we use embeddings heavily for retrieval. what's the embedding pipeline like and can we plug our vector DB?
-- 07:40 Jonah: Redwood returns embeddings in standard float32/float16 formats and we have sample connectors for common vector DBs; for private you can keep embeddings local and Redwood can expose a streaming embedding API to your vector loader. we'll share a LlamaIndex connector example.
-- 08:03 Alex: any gotchas with function calls / tool calling? will callbacks to our tools run through the connector or externally?
-- 08:12 Jonah: tool call payloads stay in your VPC when using private deployment; hosted uses secure webhook callbacks. we recommend signed webhook tokens and mutual TLS for production webhooks.
-- 08:31 Maya: ok let's talk pilot scope — we propose sandbox VPC connector + a 7-day benchmark: host one route for chat (p50 target 120ms) and one for embeddings (batched). Redwood SE to run benchmark in parallel and compare hosted vs dedicated latency and cost. Does that sound right?
-- 08:50 Alex: yes, and we'll provide traffic replay of 2 days anonymized. Priya will own that.
-- 09:00 Marcus: I want to see throttle and quota behavior under spike tests — we can do a 20% above normal traffic spike scenario.
-- 09:10 Ben: procurement note — we need explicit data residency and audit log retention details for contract.
-- 09:20 Maya: noted, will include in security package.
-- 09:30 Priya: integration questions — our codebase uses LangChain v0.1x and some internal shims. if Redwood's SDK breaks changes in LangChain we need compatibility layers. How stable are your adapters?
-- 09:44 Jonah: adapters are small shim layers. we maintain examples for LangChain (and LlamaIndex) across common versions; for edge cases we can provide an internal compatibility shim. we also have a python SDK and REST endpoint for direct calls.
-- 10:12 Alex: are there rate-limit headers returned so our gateway can reflect throttles to clients?
-- 10:18 Jonah: yes standard headers show remaining tokens/quota and reset times. we can also emit webhook alerts for quota approaches.
-- 10:35 Dana: also need pricing model for embeddings vs generation — we prefer predictable unit pricing rather than surprise bills
-- 10:43 Maya: pricing options include usage-based and reserved committed pricing for dedicated. reserved gives predictable unit cost and capacity guarantees. we'll send both illustrative sheets.
-- 11:05 Alex: one more: for private on-prem, what's the upgrade cadence and how are security patches handled?
-- 11:14 Jonah: private deployments have a customer-controlled upgrade window; Redwood issues signed images and a patching schedule. for critical CVEs we push emergency patches through the control plane and provide CVE reports.
-- 11:36 Maya: ok wrapping up — recap: Redwood to share connector guide, security/SOC docs, pricing, and a benchmark plan. schedule sandbox test week of 6/24. action items noted. anything else?
-- 11:55 Alex: no that's it, thanks.
-- 12:00 End of recording
